core_obligations: Existence for locally Noetherian $X$: combine the upstairs map $c^p_{Y/X}$ with the Tate isomorphism $c_{Y/X}$ to obtain a map $\Omega^p_{Y/\mathbf{Z}} \to f^*\Omega^p_{X/\mathbf{Z}} \otimes \omega_{Y/X}$, and read the result as a map $f_*\Omega^p_{Y/\mathbf{Z}} \to \Omega^p_{X/\mathbf{Z}}$; property (1) holds because the evaluation of $\omega_{Y/X}$ sends $\tau$ to $\operatorname{Trace}_f(1)$, and property (2) for locally Noetherian base changes follows from the compatibility of $c^p_{Y/X}$ and $c_{Y/X}$ (proof lines 4061-4097).

Uniqueness in the model case: if $X$ is smooth over $\mathbf{Z}$ and $f$ is etale over a dense open, then $\Omega^p_{X/\mathbf{Z}}$ is torsion free, so it suffices to determine $\Theta^p_{Y/X}$ over that open; there $f$ is etale, hence $f^*\Omega^p_{X/\mathbf{Z}} = \Omega^p_{Y/\mathbf{Z}}$ and the pinned composite forces uniqueness (proof lines 4100-4117).

Uniqueness in general (locally Noetherian): use the local presentation of a finite syntomic morphism as a base change of a universal finite syntomic family, whose total space is smooth with the morphism etale over a dense open, so that the map is determined by property (1) (proof lines 4119-4142).

Extension to arbitrary $X$: reduce to affine $X$ by Zariski locality (accepting the small omitted detail), write $X$ as a directed limit of Noetherian affine schemes, descend $f$ to a finite syntomic morphism over a stage, and define $\Theta^p_{Y/X}$ as the colimit of the maps on the stages, where the colimit description of the global sections is displayed (proof lines 4144-4172).

Base change compatibility in general, including the compatibility with cartesian diagrams whose base is affine, using the same limit argument and the Noetherian affine case established above (the author records this with a hint and a small omitted detail) (proof lines 4172-4184).
proof_roadmap: Existence over a locally Noetherian base (proof lines 4061-4097).
Uniqueness in the smooth-etale-over-a-dense-open model (proof lines 4100-4117).
Uniqueness via the universal finite syntomic families (proof lines 4119-4142).
Absolute Noetherian approximation: construction and compatibility (proof lines 4144-4184).
difficulty_reason: The lemma is Garel's trace map for finite syntomic morphisms: a unique rule assigning to each such morphism maps on differential forms compatible with the trace on the structure sheaf and with base change (statement lines 4037-4058). The proof builds the map over a locally Noetherian base from the upstairs Garel map and the Tate isomorphism of the determinant of the cotangent complex with the dualizing sheaf, proves uniqueness first in the smooth model where the morphism is etale over a dense open, then generally through the universal finite syntomic families, and finally extends everything beyond the Noetherian case by absolute Noetherian approximation, defining the map as a colimit over the stages. The three-stage existence-uniqueness-approximation argument is the substance, so the claim is H3.
